title: Plumbing Invoice Template Word Guide: Line-Iteming Labor, Fixtures & Trip Fees
description: Step-by-step guide to using a plumbing invoice template in Word — line-item labor, trip fees, fixtures, and fittings so your invoice is clear, defensible, and gets paid without a dispute.
h1: How to Invoice a Plumbing Job in Word (Template Walkthrough)
intro: Plumbers lose money on invoices that lump everything into one number. This walkthrough shows how to structure a plumbing invoice in Word, line by line, using the free template.

sections.h2: Why a line-itemed plumbing invoice beats a lump sum

blocks.text: A lump-sum invoice hides your pricing. The client can't tell what was labor, what was the fixture, what was the trip — and a vague invoice is the one that gets disputed. A line-itemed invoice shows each charge separately, so the client can match every dollar to the work they watched you do.
Line-itemed invoices also protect you in a dispute. Your itemized trip fee, labor hours, and fixture cost are your record of what was billed. A lump sum gives you nothing to point to.

sections.h2: The 6 line items a plumbing invoice should have

blocks.text: Not every job needs all six, but these cover most residential service calls. The Word template has these as pre-filled rows — edit the description, quantity, and rate, and delete the rows you don't need.

sections.h2: How to handle the trip fee in Word

blocks.text: The trip fee is the most disputed charge in plumbing invoicing — because plumbers hide it. Some roll it into a higher hourly rate; some add it silently to materials. Pick one method and be consistent, then show it as its own line on every invoice.
In the Word template, the trip fee is the first row: 'Trip / service call — 1 each @ $95.' State it upfront when you book the job and it never surprises anyone on the invoice.

sections.h2: Marking up fixtures vs passing through at cost

blocks.text: Pass the fixture through at your exact cost, or mark it up 15-25% to cover sourcing, pickup, and warranty handling. Both are legitimate — the mistake is being inconsistent or hiding the markup.

If you mark up, show one line: 'Kitchen faucet (Moen 87233) — 1 @ $145.' If you pass through at cost, show the same line at your cost and add a separate 'Materials handling — 15%' line so the charge is visible.

sections.h2: Editing the Word template: the 4 things to change first

items: Business name, license number, and phone in the header — clients check the license number on every plumbing invoice
Tax rate cell — look up your state's rule (some tax labor, some tax only materials, some exempt residential repairs)
Line-item rows — delete unused rows, edit quantities and rates on the ones you did use
Payment terms line — Net 15 vs Due on receipt vs COD

sections.h2: Download the plumbing invoice template (Word, Excel, PDF)

blocks.text: The free plumbing invoice template comes in three formats. The Word version is easiest to edit and brand with your logo. The Excel version auto-calculates tax and totals. The PDF is print-ready for hand-filled invoices on the truck. All three are pre-filled with plumbing line items.

faq.q: Should I charge a trip fee on every plumbing invoice?
faq.a: Yes, as a visible line item. The trip fee covers travel time and fuel. Hiding it in a padded hourly rate causes disputes. Show it as 'Trip / service call — 1 @ $95' and state it when you book the job.

faq.q: Do I need my plumbing license number on the invoice?
faq.a: In most states, yes. Put it in the header next to your business name.
